name: North Saanich

facts.text: North Saanich adopted Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548 on October 3, 2022, replacing Bylaw No. 935 (1999). Removing any tree it regulates needs a permit.
facts.sourceTitle: Trees | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: The District has adopted a new Tree Protection Bylaw that came into effect on October 3, 2022.
facts.note: V3: confirmed on the live page (https://www.northsaanich.ca/node/51 redirects here). The old excerpt quoted 'Bylaw No. 1548', which is on the Residential Tree Permit Guide, not this page, so it was replaced with a verbatim sentence from this page. Bylaw PDF, verbatim: 'FINALLY PASSED AND ADOPTED the 3rd day of October, 2022' and 'District of North Saanich Tree Protection By-law No. 935, 1999 and all bylaws amending the said bylaw are hereby repealed.' Same page, verbatim: 'A tree permit is required to remove any trees regulated by the District's Tree Protection Bylaw'.

facts.text: In North Saanich a regulated tree is generally one 20 cm or more in diameter at breast height (measured 1.4 m above grade), plus protected trees at smaller sizes (see ns-tree-protected-10cm). Significant trees are those 60 cm or more. Staff inspect before a permit is issued and may require replacement trees.
facts.sourceTitle: Residential Tree Permit Guide (District of North Saanich, November 2024)
facts.excerpt: A tree with a D.B.H. of 20 cm or greater
facts.note: V3: confirmed on the live PDF (northsaanich.ca/wp-content/uploads/... redirects to www.northsaanich.ca/media/file/ns-residential-tree-permit-guide-web-final-v1). The guide is dated November 2024. Same guide, verbatim: 'a. A significant tree with a D.B.H. of 60 cm or greater' and 'District staff will conduct an inspection'. The trees page FAQ adds that the 60 cm significant-tree rule excludes 'cottonwood, red alder and Pacific willow'. Note: the guide still cites the old OCP Bylaw No. 1130 for DPAs; the trees page links the current OCP Bylaw No. 1587.

facts.text: North Saanich protects arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood, Pacific (western) yew and shore or lodgepole pine from 10 cm DBH, and any tree from 10 cm DBH growing in an environmental or steep-slope Development Permit Area. Nesting trees, replacement trees and District trees of any size are also protected. A protected tree needs an acceptable reason for removal (for example dead or dying, within 2 m of a foundation, invasive, or needed for a principal building) and cannot be removed under the annual allowance.
facts.sourceTitle: Trees | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: Tree with a D.B.H. of 10 cm or greater growing in an environmental or steep slope Development Permit Area (DPA)
facts.note: V3: NEW. This VERIFIES the research/areas.json claim that trees are regulated from 10 cm in environmental and steep-slope DPAs (V1 had left it unverified because the host was blocked). Same page, verbatim: 'Arbutus, Garry Oak, Pacific Dogwood, Pacific or Western Yew, or Shore or Lodge Pole Pine with a D.B.H. of 10 cm or greater' and 'Protected trees cannot be removed under the annual allowance.' The acceptable reasons are from the same page's FAQ ('when the tree is within two meters of a building foundation', 'when it is an invasive species').

facts.text: North Saanich tree permits take about 2-3 weeks of staff review once the application is complete. Do not book the work before the permit is issued, and post the permit on the property at least 48 hours before cutting. Where replacement trees are required (generally two per tree removed, three per significant tree), the owner pays a refundable security and notifies the District once they are planted.
facts.sourceTitle: Trees | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: Once your completed application is submitted anticipate 2-3 weeks for staff review and permit issuance. Do not schedule a contractor before obtaining the permit.
facts.note: V3: NEW; confirms the review time and posting rule already in content/areas/north-saanich.json. Same page, verbatim: 'Please display the permit in a visible location at least 48 hours prior to commencing work.', 'Two replacement trees for every tree removed' and 'three replacement trees for every significant tree removed'. The page lists permit fees and the guide lists a per-tree deposit; no dollar figures are used here (CONTRACT).

facts.text: Topping is prohibited under North Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw. If a tree in imminent danger of falling is cut before a permit is issued, the owner must notify the District and file a retroactive application; under section 5 the cut must be reported by the next business day and the tree left on the lot until the District has visited.
facts.sourceTitle: Trees | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: Topping trees is not an acceptable arboricultural practice and is prohibited in bylaws throughout the region, including in North Saanich’s current Tree Protection Bylaw.
facts.note: V3: CORRECTED source. 'Topping is prohibited' is NOT in the Residential Tree Permit Guide (the old sourceUrl), and the old excerpt was a paraphrase; the wording is on the trees page FAQ, so the source moved there. Same page, verbatim: 'Notification to the District and a retroactive application would be required.' Bylaw No. 1548 s.5.1, verbatim: 'shall report the Cutting to the Director within the next business day' and 'shall not Remove the Tree from the lot until the District has visited the lot'. Re-topping: s.4.1(i) exempts 'Re-topping of a tree that does not cause Damage to the tree', while the FAQ says a previously topped tree 'can be re-topped with a tree permit if is creating a high or extreme risk'; ask the District before re-topping.

facts.text: North Saanich allows pruning without a permit (for example crown lifting or window pruning) when it follows sound arboricultural practice, and the bylaw does not regulate hedge pruning. Pruning that counts as 'Damage' under Bylaw 1548 needs a permit: topping, removing more than 25% of a tree's live crown in any 12-month period, or lift pruning that leaves the live crown at less than 50% of the tree's height.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548, 2022 (District of North Saanich)
facts.excerpt: Removing more than twenty five (25) percent of the live Crown of a Tree in any twelve (12) month period;
facts.note: V3: NEW. Bylaw s.2 'Damage' definition (items a-d) and s.3.1 ('no person shall Cut, Damage or Remove any Tree or Protected Tree ... unless a Tree Permit has been issued'). Same bylaw, verbatim: 'lift Pruning where the lower branches of the live Crown (green branches) of the Tree are Removed to reduce the live Crown to less than fifty (50) percent of the total Tree height'. Trees page FAQ, verbatim: 'Pruning of trees (such as crown lifting or window pruning) is allowed without a permit so long as it is done in accordance with arboricultural best practices.' and 'No, the bylaw does not regulate the pruning of hedges'.

facts.text: North Saanich's tree bylaw does not apply to trees cut in the Agricultural Land Reserve for an agricultural use, but only if the owner first files a commissioned affidavit and an arborist report with the District showing the farm use cannot go elsewhere on the lot.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548, 2022 (District of North Saanich)
facts.excerpt: Trees that are Cut or Removed within the Agricultural Land Reserve established under the Agricultural Land Commission Act, provided that the Owner files with the District a commissioned affidavit
facts.note: V3: NEW (s.4.1(a)). Same clause continues, verbatim: 'and an Arborist Report verifying that the purpose of Cutting or Removal of a Tree is to enable the land on which the Trees are growing to be used for an Agricultural Use'. Relevant to the many ALR acreages (see ns-alr-rural). Clearing for landscaping is not an agricultural use.

facts.text: North Saanich's 2025 OCP (Bylaw No. 1587, section 5.10) sets five Development Permit Areas: DPA 1 Marine Uplands and Foreshore, DPA 2 Creeks, Wetlands, Riparian Areas and Significant Water Resources, DPA 3 Sensitive Ecosystems, DPA 4 Steep Slopes, and DPA 5 Commercial, Industrial and Multi-Family. Development and site alteration in them may need a development permit, and a property can be in more than one.
facts.sourceTitle: Development Permits | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: The District has recently adopted a new Official Community Plan that includes five Development Permit Areas (DPAs).
facts.note: V3: CORRECTED. The old text listed only DPAs 1, 3 and 4, and the old excerpt is not on the page. The old URL (northsaanich.ca/business-development/development-applications/development-permit/) redirects here. Same page, verbatim: 'Development and site alteration located in these five Development Permit Areas may be subject to the issuance of a Development Permit.' Application requirements on the page include a biologist report (DPA 1, 2, 3), a geotechnical report (DPA 4), and an arborist report with a tree management and replacement plan.

facts.text: North Saanich's Marine Uplands and Foreshore DPA covers all land within 15 m of the ocean's natural boundary (measured both landward and seaward), plus Queen Mary Bay, Gullhaven, Tsehum Harbour and Lagoon, and marinas. Its Steep Slopes DPA covers slopes over 30% across at least a 6 m run, plus land within 10 m of the top or toe of such slopes.
facts.sourceTitle: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 1587 (District of North Saanich, April 2025)
facts.excerpt: All lands within 15 metres, measured horizontally in both landward and seaward directions, from the natural boundary of the ocean
facts.note: V3: NEW (s.5.10.2 designation (a) and s.5.10.5 designation). Same PDF, verbatim: 'All lands within North Saanich with slopes exceeding 30% over a minimum 6-metre run and all lands within 10-metres of the top-of-bank or toe-of-slope of such features'. Mapped areas are 'shown generally' on the DPA maps, so a site check is still needed.

facts.text: In North Saanich's riparian (DPA 2), sensitive ecosystem (DPA 3) and steep slope (DPA 4) areas, routine maintenance of existing lawns, landscaped areas and pathways needs no development permit, but redeveloping decks, hardscaped patios or non-native landscaped areas is not exempt. In the foreshore area (DPA 1), gardening and yard maintenance such as mowing, pruning, planting and minor soil disturbance that does not change the land's contours is exempt. Invasive removal is exempt in DPA 2 and 3 only by hand, without power tools, with the area replanted in native species.
facts.sourceTitle: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 1587 (District of North Saanich, April 2025)
facts.excerpt: Routine maintenance of existing lawns, landscaped areas, and pathways but does not include the redevelopment of existing decks, hardscaped patios, or non-native landscaped areas
facts.note: V3: NEW (s.5.10.3.1(d), 5.10.4.1(e), 5.10.5.1(c); DPA 1 s.5.10.2.1(e) and (f); invasive removal s.5.10.3.1(c), 5.10.4.1(d)). DPA 1, verbatim: 'gardening and yard maintenance activities, such as lawn mowing, tree and shrub pruning, vegetation planting and minor soil disturbances that do not alter the contours of the land'. DPA 2/3, verbatim: 'the work is done by hand and without the use of any motorized or power-assisted tools, equipment or machinery'. Tree removal in these areas still needs a tree permit (ns-tree-protected-10cm).

facts.text: Nearly 35% of North Saanich is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and its OCP aims to keep the community's rural, agricultural and marine character. Acreages and hobby farms are typical lot types.
facts.sourceTitle: Agriculture & Environment | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: nearly 35% of the District is within the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR)
facts.note: V3: confirmed on the live page (northsaanich.ca/your-community/agriculture-land-security/ redirects here). Same page, verbatim: 'As of March 2019 there were 125 parcels classified as farm by BC Assessment.' OCP Bylaw 1587 goal 3.3.1, verbatim: 'Retains and enhances the rural, agricultural, and marine character of the community.' 'Acreages and hobby farms are typical' is our framing.

facts.text: North Saanich has provincial groundwater observation wells. In the October 2026 report, a bedrock well there was at the low end of its historical range, which matters to properties on private wells.
facts.sourceTitle: West Coast Groundwater Report (BC River Forecast Centre)
facts.excerpt: a crystalline bedrock well reads at the low end of its historical range
facts.note: V3 UNVERIFIED: bcrfc.env.gov.bc.ca is still refused by this session's network (CONNECT 403, retried after 30 s). The excerpt is a paraphrase from a search snippet. The report changes over time, so do not quote a reading. prov-private-well-drought (verified) covers the advice. The District's own drought documents (Agriculture & Environment page) are regional and do not mention North Saanich wells.

facts.text: North Saanich's municipal water comes from the CRD-operated Saanich Peninsula Water System and runs through District water mains to a meter at each property line. CRD Stage 1 watering schedules apply in the District from May 1 to September 30. Properties on private wells follow provincial well guidance instead (see prov-private-well-drought).
facts.sourceTitle: Water, Sewer & Drainage | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: The District's municipal water is supplied through the Saanich Peninsula Water System, which is operated by the Capital Regional District (CRD).
facts.note: V3: CORRECTED source. The old source (node/58, Water Conservation) supports the watering-schedule part only; the supply and mains part is on this page. Same page, verbatim: 'Water mains run underground below the streets and boulevards throughout North Saanich and connect to the water meter at the property line of your home.' Water Conservation page (https://www.northsaanich.ca/lands-planning/agriculture-environment/water-conservation, node/58 redirects there), verbatim: 'Corresponding watering schedules are in effect within the District of North Saanich (and all other regional water supply system areas).' The private-wells sentence is our framing; no parcel map of well vs. municipal supply was found.

facts.text: North Saanich encourages owners to reduce or stop cosmetic pesticide use, and says it has eliminated pesticide use on municipal property for over a decade. This review did not confirm whether a residential pesticide bylaw applies, so check with the District before advising.
facts.sourceTitle: Pesticide Use | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: encourages property owners to reduce or eliminate the cosmetic use of pesticides on their properties
facts.note: V3: confirmed on the live page (node/57 redirects here). Same page, verbatim: 'Through the pest management process, the District has been able to eliminate pesticide use for over a decade.' The page also lists free leftover-pesticide drop-off at Hartland Landfill and Ellice Recycle. The District's Bylaws & Policies list returned no result for 'pesticide' on 2026-11-21; that is NOT evidence that no bylaw exists, so do not say so.

facts.text: Any outdoor burning in North Saanich needs a permit bought from the North Saanich Fire Department, and burning is allowed only on scheduled burning days in the season (open with a permit from November 5, 2026 for 2026-2027). No burning is allowed in the Dean Park area, other than outdoor fire appliances. Check the District's current calendar before burning.
facts.sourceTitle: Burning in North Saanich | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: Any outdoor burning in North Saanich requires the purchase of a permit from the North Saanich Fire Department
facts.note: V3: NEW; closes the R1a burning gap. Same page, verbatim: 'Burning Season - OPEN NOV. 5, 2026 (with permit)' and 'No burning is allowed in the Dean Park area located west of East Saanich Road, south of Forest Park Drive'. TIME-BOUND: the season status and calendar change yearly; re-check at publish time. The page lists permit rates; no dollar figures are used here.

facts.text: North Saanich's burning regulations (September 2024) allow open burning only on the first and third Thursday, Friday and Saturday of each month in the season, sunrise to sunset. Piles up to 10 x 10 x 10 ft must be at least 25 ft from a property line and 50 ft from structures; larger machine-stacked piles need 50 ft and 100 ft and a 'Good' venting index. Leaves, green grass and weeds may not be burned.
facts.sourceTitle: Burning Regulations (District of North Saanich, September 2024)
facts.excerpt: Open air burning shall only take place on the first and third consecutive Thursday, Friday, and Saturday during the burning season from sunrise to sunset.
facts.note: V3: NEW. Same PDF, verbatim: 'All piles up to 10’ x 10’ x 10’ must be a minimum 25’ from a property line and 50’ from any structures or combustibles.' The prohibited-materials list includes 'All Leaves' and 'Green Grass & Weeds'. 'Weed torches are not permitted'. The PDF lists permit fees; no dollar figures are used here. The 2026-2027 calendar PDF linked from the burning page marks the actual burning days.

facts.text: North Saanich's Green Waste Facility (10180 Littlewood Road) is open on select Thursdays and most Saturdays, 8 a.m. to noon. It takes clean branches, grass clippings, garden debris and hand-loadable stumps, but not wood waste or loads with rocks or soil. Contractors must show the green waste came from a North Saanich property, for example with a letter from the owner.
facts.sourceTitle: Green Waste | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: Contractors must provide proof that the green waste came from a North Saanich property, for example, a letter from the property owner
facts.note: V3: NEW. Same page, verbatim: 'Green Waste must be clean and free of debris such as rocks and soil.' and 'Wood waste not allowed'. The page lists rates; no dollar figures are used here. Invasive plants: follow the CRD rule (crd-invasive-disposal); the page does not say whether invasives are accepted.

facts.text: North Saanich's Noise Bylaw No. 1383 (2015) bars operating any machine or engine in a way that disturbs neighbours except Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. (not on statutory holidays) and Saturday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. It lists no permitted hours on Sundays.
facts.sourceTitle: Noise Bylaw No. 1383 (2015) (District of North Saanich)
facts.excerpt: Monday to Friday inclusive between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. of each day
facts.note: V3: NEW (s.12, headed 'PROHIBITIONS RELATED TO CONSTRUCTION', which also covers 'operate any kind of machine or engine'). Found through the District's Bylaws & Policies search. The PDF is a scanned copy with OCR errors; it reads 'Saturday between the hours of 8:00 am. to 4:00 p.m.' The bylaw lists fines; no dollar figures are used here. Applies to mowers, blowers and other powered equipment only where the noise disturbs; confirm with the District for Sunday work.

facts.text: North Saanich has a Community Wildfire Protection Plan (first prepared in 2011, revised in 2021), and its Fire Department arranges FireSmart home and property assessments. More than 50 assessments were done in 2018-2019, mostly in Dean Park, and BC Parks has done fuel work in John Dean Provincial Park.
facts.sourceTitle: FireSmart Wildfire Prevention | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: The District has completed over 50 FireSmart home and property assessments over the past two years. A majority of these assessments were located in the Dean Park neighbourhood.
facts.note: V3: NEW; closes the R1a wildfire-interface gap. 'Past two years' refers to 2018-2019 on the page. Same page, verbatim: '2021: After a process of community engagement, the District prepared a revised CWPP'. The page's top banner (campfire ban lifted September 3, 2026) is TIME-BOUND and should not be quoted.

facts.text: North Saanich asks residents to put away garbage, birdseed, compost and pet food and to keep fallen fruit off the ground to avoid wildlife conflicts. The District is a member of the Capital Region Invasive Species Partnership (CRISP); invasive plants on private land are reported to CRISP.
facts.sourceTitle: Wildlife & Invasive Species | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: put garbage, birdseed, compost and pet food away and to keep fruit from trees off the ground
facts.note: V3: NEW. Same page, verbatim: 'The District of North Saanich is a member of the Capital Region Invasive Species Partnership'. The page does not mention deer; the deer gap stays open.
